cards.title: Introduction to OOP
cards.content:
Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) is a programming paradigm that uses classes and objects to practice code reusability, organization, and modularity.

Python is a multi-paradigm language, meaning it fully supports OOP principles.

cards.title: Classes and Objects
cards.content:
A class is a blueprint for creating objects, while an object is an instance of a class.

class Car:
    def __init__(self, brand):
        self.brand = brand

my_car = Car("Toyota")
print(my_car.brand)  # Output: Toyota

options.text: An object is the blueprint of a class.
A class is an instance of an object.

Classes and objects are unrelated concepts.

cards.title: The Four Pillars of OOP
cards.content:
Object-Oriented Programming relies on four fundamental principles:

  • Encapsulation: Bundling data and methods that work on that data within one unit.
  • Inheritance: Creating a new class from an existing class to reuse code.
  • Polymorphism: Using a uniform interface for different data types or classes.
  • Abstraction: Hiding complex implementation details and showing only the essential features.

Restricting direct access to data using private variables
Allowing different classes to have methods with the same name
Hiding internal details and exposing only necessary features

cards.title: Inheritance in Python
cards.content:
Inheritance allows a class (child class) to inherit attributes and methods from another class (parent class).

class Animal:
    def speak(self):
        return "Animal speaks"

class Dog(Animal):
    def speak(self):
        return "Woof!"

d = Dog()
print(d.speak())  # Output: Woof!

cards.title: OOP Summary
cards.content:
You have learned the core concepts of Object-Oriented Programming in Python:

  • Classes and Objects
  • The __init__ constructor
  • The Four Pillars: Encapsulation, Inheritance, Polymorphism, and Abstraction

Use these principles to write clean, modular, and maintainable Python applications.
